result.title: SARGO: Agreement-Gated Reinforcement and Suppression via On-Policy Self-Guidance for Visual Hallucination Mitigation
result.summary: Vision-language models remain susceptible to visual hallucinations, often mixing grounded information with unsupported claims in the same response. Response-level reinforcement learning assigns a shared advantage to all tokens in a response, causing negative updates to suppress correct information alongside unsupported claims. To reduce hallucination while preserving useful visual information, we introduce SARGO (Self-guided Advantage-Routed Grounding Optimization), a post-training framework for selective reinforcement and suppression through on-policy self-guidance. Direct and reciprocal weighting gives better-supported tokens stronger reinforcement on positive updates and weaker penalties on negative updates. Agreement between overall and hallucination-specific advantages selects when to apply this guidance. At the response level, a reference-calibrated reward couples factuality with the retention and expansion of grounded information, discouraging lower hallucination scores obtained through omission. Experiments on Qwen3-VL-4B, Qwen3-VL-8B, and Gemma3-4B demonstrate that SARGO outperforms the evaluated mitigation baselines across Obj-Hal, AMBER, THRONE, and SHR evaluations. SARGO achieves these gains while preserving useful visual information and general multimodal capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SARGO 后训练框架，通过 on-policy 自引导对 token 做优势路由，配合整体优势与幻觉专用优势的一致性门控以及参考校准的响应级奖励，在降低视觉幻觉的同时保留有用视觉信息。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 token 级信用分配与「避免因抑制幻觉而丢失正确视觉信息」的取向，直接关联 LVR 中的贡献分配与视觉证据保留问题；但监督只在输出 token 层，未涉及内部 latent 状态，可供核查能否迁移为对 latent 证据使用的细粒度奖励。
